discovery: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac

nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitat Munchen, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Feynman's dream of a quantum simulator became reality through ultracold atoms in optical lattices. In 1998 Jaksch, Bruder, Cirac, Gardiner and Zoller showed that cold bosons in a laser-made lattice realise the Bose-Hubbard model and can be driven from a superfluid to a Mott insulator. In 2002 Greiner, Mandel, Esslinger, Hansch and Bloch observed this quantum phase transition, opening a new era in which strongly correlated condensed-matter Hamiltonians are engineered, tuned and read out atom by atom. Zoller and Cirac supplied the unifying theoretical framework, including proposals for artificial gauge fields, lattice gauge theories and entanglement generation; Bloch's group pioneered controlled experiments on many-body localisation, quantum magnetism, out-of-equilibrium dynamics and single-site-resolved microscopy. This work unites quantum optics, condensed matter and quantum information, is used by hundreds of laboratories worldwide, and underpins today's analog quantum simulators and neutral-atom quantum computers.
